title: HA/DR automation: multi-AZ Terraform + Helm updates, runbooks-as-code, and restore drill automation
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: make Redwood Private installer fully multi-AZ and provide repeatable, automated HA/DR drills and runbooks-as-code so customers can validate failover, restore, and upgrades with minimal manual steps. This PR implements Terraform and Helm changes to support multi-AZ deployments, adds an opinionated upgrade/rollback automation flow, and introduces runbooks-as-code + a drill runner for scheduled restore drills.

What changed (high level):
- Terraform: updated the vpc module to support AZ-aware subnets, route tables, and NAT/gateway placement; added optional route-policy for cross-AZ failover and lightweight health checks for bastion/egress. New variables: multi_az_enabled, az_count, az_routing_policy. Includes idempotent drift-safe migration plan helpers.
- Helm charts (redwood-helm-charts): topology-aware pod anti-affinity, topologySpreadConstraints, updated StatefulSet templates for zone-aware PVC provisioning (storageClass parameterization), PodDisruptionBudgets for critical services, and configurable readiness/terminationGracePeriod tuning for faster controlled failovers.
- Installer orchestration: installer supports deploying across N AZs (default 3) with zone-aware node selectors and a new preflight check that validates AZ health and storage topology.
- Runbooks-as-code: added runbooks/ directory with Playbooks (yaml) that encode common HA/DR procedures: simulated AZ failure, control plane failover, etc. Playbooks are executable by the new drill-runner utility.
- Drill automation: drill-runner (bash+go shim) that executes preflight, failover simulation (via terraform taint/route updates or node cordon), verification checks (application routing + KV cache consistency), and optional restore from snapshot. Includes a dry-run and a --pause-before-rollback flag.
- Upgrade/rollback tooling: canary rolling upgrade step added to installer pipeline with automatic SLO/metric checks (latency error budget) and automatic rollback on regression. Integrates with observability-pack to query key metrics and trigger rollback via helm rollback or terraform rollback hooks.
- Tests & CI: added integration tests that run in perf-canary environment to validate node failure simulation and verify application-level invariants (requests per second, tail latency). CI pipeline updated to run runbook lints and terraform plan checks.

Checklist:
- [x] Terraform multi-AZ module and migration helper
- [x] Helm chart updates (affinity, PDBs, topologySpread)
- [x] Installer orchestration changes and preflight checks
- [x] Runbooks-as-code and drill-runner utility
- [x] Canary upgrade + automatic rollback wiring
- [x] Integration tests and CI gating
- [x] Docs: added runbook README and quickstart for performing a scheduled drill

Notes & migration guidance:
- Existing single-AZ deployments are unaffected by default. To migrate: enable multi_az_enabled=true and follow the migration helper in modules/vpc/README.md. The migration helper generates a safe terraform plan that creates AZ subnets and migrates NAT/gateway objects with minimal downtime.
- StorageClass must support topology-aware provisioning for zone-local PVs. If unavailable, installer will fall back to cross-AZ PVs with a warning and require a manual restore modality.

Related work: Linear ENG-2043 (multi-AZ installer), SRE-118 (drill automation), PM-452 (DR runbooks). Related PRs: redwood-helm-charts#881 (chart refactors), redwood-terraform#134.

Backwards compatibility: designed to be opt-in. There are feature gates for multi_az_enabled and drill automation to avoid surprising existing customers.

Testing summary:
- Local unit tests for terraform helpers and runbook linter: pass
- Integration (perf-canary) runs: 3/4 pass on first run — one flaky test was fixed by reducing timeouts in readiness probes.
- CI: terraform plan and helm lint are required checks.

Follow-ups:
- Scheduler for periodic drills (separate PR)
- Add S3-compatible snapshot automation for on-prem customers
- Documentation site pages for multi-AZ migration guides

This PR is fairly large but broken into logical commits and files to make review incremental. See commits_summary and files_changed for details.

review_conversation: Ethan Chen: Overall looks solid. Two questions: i) how do we ensure storage topology for on-prem; ii) what happens to existing single-AZ clusters during migration?

Maya Patel (author): For storage we validate storageClass topology and fall back to cross-AZ PVs with an explicit warning, documented in modules/vpc/README.md. Migration uses the helper which creates new subnets and migrates NAT/gateway objects with a planned cutover; I've added a migration checklist in the README.
Rachel Kim: Can we add a flag to skip automated rollback if customers want manual control?
Maya Patel: Added --no-auto-rollback flag to canary step and documented behavior in installer/steps/upgrade_canary.go.
release_notes: Adds opt-in multi-AZ support for installer, Helm chart updates for zone-awareness, runbooks-as-code and automated HA/DR drill runner, and canary upgrade with automatic rollback. Backwards compatible and opt-in.
